title: Homogeneous translation symmetry at a near point without reducedness
statement:
Let $F$ be a field of any characteristic and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative $F$-algebra essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a prime ideal, assume $A=R/I$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], and assume that no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$ (a minimal prime is a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime). Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and $S=(\operatorname{gr}_I R)\otimes_A k$, and assume $\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ and let $y\in Y$ lie over the closed point [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Identify this fibre with $\operatorname{Proj}S$ [def-pc-proj]. Set $R_y=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_y$, and set
$$h_R(n)=\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}),\quad h_y(n)=\operatorname{length}_{R_y}(R_y/\mathfrak n_y^{n+1}),\quad \delta=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(y)$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-length, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field], and $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$. Assume $\Lambda^\delta h_y=h_R$.
For any graded surjection $P=k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_N]\twoheadrightarrow S$, with variables of degree one, let $K$ be its homogeneous kernel and let $\mathfrak q_y\subset P$ be the inverse image of the homogeneous prime representing $y$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. There exists a proper homogeneous ideal $L\subseteq\mathfrak q_y$ such that, in polynomial rings on disjoint variable tuples $Z,W$,
$$f(0)=0,\quad f(-Z)\in L(Z),\quad f(Z+W)\in L(Z)+L(W)\quad(f\in L),$$
$$g(Z+W)\in K(Z)+L(W)\quad(g\in K).$$
Here $L(Z)$, $L(W)$ and $K(Z)$ mean the ideals generated by the indicated substitutions in the larger polynomial ring. Thus the assertion records the equations of a homogeneous additive subgroup and its translation action on the normal-cone fibre; it does not assert that $L$ is generated in degree one. No reducedness is assumed on $R$.

source.place: Cossart--Jannsen--Saito, Canonical embedded and non-embedded resolution of singularities for excellent two-dimensional schemes, March 12 2009 preprint, section 2 (X any excellent scheme, no reducedness): the characteristic-independent subgroup scheme B_{P,x'} and its action in the proof of Theorem 2.14, printed p.36, using the near condition of Definition 2.13 / Theorem 2.10(2), printed pp.32--33, and the normal-cone comparison of Theorem 2.2(2)(ii), printed p.28. The cited originals are Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, Theorem IV, and Additive groups associated with points of a projective space, Theorem 2. Read online at https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/13766/1/MP32.pdf; archival copy WANTED. The document field names the ancestor (BMT) source only. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Reduce the given presentation to a minimal one. The degree-one map $P_1\to S_1$ is surjective: since the map is graded, the degree-one part of any preimage of an element of $S_1$ is a preimage. Choose a basis $V_1,\ldots,V_r$ of its kernel and lift a basis of $S_1$ to $X_1,\ldots,X_e$. The invertible linear change gives $P=k[X,V]=Q[V]$, $Q=k[X]$. Its inverse is the inverse matrix substitution, by the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The map $Q\to S$ is surjective because $S$ is generated by $S_1$ [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. With $J=\ker(Q\to S)$ and $\mathfrak q_0$ the inverse image of $y$, evaluation at $V=0$ shows $K=(V)+JP$ and $\mathfrak q_y=(V)+\mathfrak q_0P$: a polynomial minus its value at $V=0$ belongs to $(V)$. In particular the presentation $Q\to S$ has bijective degree-one map. Linear substitutions commute with addition, negation and evaluation at zero, so an ideal satisfying the desired formulas in $(X,V)$ coordinates gives one in the original coordinates by the inverse substitution. Here $e\ge1$: otherwise $S_1=0$, hence $S=k$, whose Proj has no point, contrary to $y$. Thus also $N\ge1$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-scheme-near-point-order-generators] to this minimal presentation. Its local algebra, prime center, regular quotient, flat associated graded ring, non-component condition, point, residue fields and raw near equality are exactly those assumed here; that node imposes no reducedness assumption. It gives generators $H\in J_d$, $d>0$, with $H/1\in(\mathfrak q_0Q_{\mathfrak q_0})^d$. In $P$, define $U_d=\{f\in P_d:f/1\in(\mathfrak q_yP_{\mathfrak q_y})^d\}$ and $U=\bigoplus U_d$. The subgroup input [lem-trf-projective-order-algebra-additive-generators] says $U=k[T]$, where $T$ is its positive-degree homogeneous additive polynomials. Its hypotheses hold: $\mathfrak q_y$ is a homogeneous prime not containing $P_+$ because it represents a projective point [def-pc-proj].

Step 2 also uses the existing order-algebra input, Dietel 9.1.3-9.1.4, pp.107-108.

proof.text: The inclusion $Q\to P$ induces a local homomorphism $Q_{\mathfrak q_0}\to P_{\mathfrak q_y}$: every denominator outside $\mathfrak q_0$ remains outside $\mathfrak q_y$, since $\mathfrak q_y\cap Q=\mathfrak q_0$. It takes $\mathfrak q_0Q_{\mathfrak q_0}$ into $\mathfrak q_yP_{\mathfrak q_y}$ and hence takes its $d$th power into the $d$th power, by multiplying fractions [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Thus each of the generators $H$ from Step 2 lies in $U_d$. Also each $V_i\in U_1$. Since $K=(V)+JP$, these $H$ and $V_i$ generate $K$ and are all in $U$. This only uses containment of powers under a local map; no equality of orders under a residue-field extension is assumed. If $J=0$, this assertion only needs the redundant variables $V_i$; if there are none, the generating family is empty.

proof.text: Set $L=(T)\subset P$. This is an ideal construction from the set $T$ of Step 2. It is homogeneous because its generators are homogeneous: decompose each coefficient of a finite sum $\sum a_it_i$ by degree and take the required total-degree part. For $t\in T\cap P_d$, $d>0$, its defining local-power condition implies $t/1\in\mathfrak q_yP_{\mathfrak q_y}$. Clearing a denominator gives $st\in\mathfrak q_y$ with $s\notin\mathfrak q_y$, so primality gives $t\in\mathfrak q_y$. Hence $L\subseteq\mathfrak q_y$, so $L$ is proper. Every $t\in T$ has positive degree, so $t(0)=0$. Evaluation at zero of any finite sum $\sum a_it_i$ therefore vanishes.

proof.text: For each additive generator $t\in T$, $t(Z+W)=t(Z)+t(W)$ and $t(-Z)=-t(Z)$; the latter follows by setting $W=-Z$ in the former and using $t(0)=0$. If $f=\sum a_it_i\in L$, substitution gives $f(-Z)=-\sum a_i(-Z)t_i(Z)\in L(Z)$ and $f(Z+W)=\sum a_i(Z+W)(t_i(Z)+t_i(W))\in L(Z)+L(W)$. These are polynomial identities over the original field in every characteristic, not assertions only about rational points.

proof.text:
In $k[Z,W]/L(W)$ every $t\in T$ satisfies $t(Z+W)=t(Z)$. Every $u\in U=k[T]$ is a polynomial expression over $k$ in finitely many such $t$, so substituting these congruences gives $u(Z+W)\equiv u(Z)\pmod {L(W)}$. Write any $g\in K$ as a finite sum $g=\sum a_i H_i$, where the $H_i$ are the generators in $K\cap U$ supplied by Step 3 (including the $V_i$). Then
$$g(Z+W)\equiv\sum_i a_i(Z+W)H_i(Z)\pmod {L(W)}.$$
The right side lies in $K(Z)$, since each $H_i\in K$. This proves $g(Z+W)\in K(Z)+L(W)$. Finally apply the inverse linear change of Step 1 to $L$. The two substitution homomorphisms agree on every variable with that change followed by addition (and likewise inversion and zero), so every displayed ideal inclusion pulls back to the requested one for the original tuple $Z$.
